Standard Library, Error Handling, and async Compared

This page aligns Rust and SLA item by item on the three things you encounter most often: Result/Option/? error handling, async/await, and how the standard library surface (containers, smart pointers, IO) lands in sa_std. All conclusions are taken from measured documents in the repository (rust_vs_sla_final_cn.md v0.2 / 2026-06-15, std_surface_metadata_cn.md v0.1 / 2026-07-01); wherever there are numbers, the framing is noted, and they do not constitute permanent guarantees.

Error Handling: Result / Option / ? / panic

Rust and SLA are consistent in the shape of error handling: both are explicit, return-value-driven error models, with no exceptions and no throw. The differences are concentrated in spelling details and the form of panic.

CapabilityRustSLA current
Result<T, E>Provided by stdProvided by sa_std
Option<T>Provided by stdProvided by sa_std
? error propagation suffixFully supportedLanded
panicpanic!("string")panic(numeric code); the string variant goes through sa_std's panic_msg
NoteSLA has no unwind / panic catch. The Drop trait is likewise not supported — cleanup is done by the compiler implicitly injecting the release primitive, and users cannot write impl Drop on the user surface.

Real code looks like this (demos/rosetta/19_result_question/main.sla, which corresponds almost line by line with main.rs in the same directory and is a direct 1:1 mapping marked ✅ in demo.md):

@import "sa_std/core/result.sa"

fn triple_ok(x: i32) -> Result<i32, i32> {
    Ok(x * 3)
}

fn compute() -> Result<i32, i32> {
    let value = triple_ok(7)?;
    Ok(value)
}

Methods Already Registered on the Standard Library Surface

The methods below have already been registered as lowering rules in sla_std/std_surface.sla_meta (source: std_surface_metadata_cn.md v0.1 / 2026-07-01 §3.2, §3.3):

TypeRegistered constructors and methods
Option<T>Some / None constructors; is_some / is_none / get / unwrap / unwrap_or
Result<T,E>Ok / Err constructors; is_ok / is_err / unwrap / unwrap_or
Vec<T>Vec::new, len, push, fallible remove, index read/write v[i] / &mut v[i]
Box/Rc/Arc::new, clone (Rc/Arc), get, as_ptr
RefCell/Cell::new; Cell::get / Cell::set

The metadata table only registers the part of the surface that “needs compiler-composed macros”; it is not a complete capability list for the standard library. Combinators such as map are not in the rule table, but go through sa_std's contracts and macro paths: Some(3).map(|x| x + 5).unwrap_or(0) in demos/rosetta/18_option_map/main.sla runs directly, and is registered in demo.md as a ✅ direct 1:1.

Fallible Methods: the ok Register + panic Code

Any std method that can fail is described with a dedicated rule kind, fallible_method: the success flag is written to the ok register for branch checking, and on failure it follows a numeric code via panic=N. The only current instance is Vec::remove:

fallible_method Vec remove sa_std/vec.sa VEC_REMOVE ok,out,receiver,index,elem_size deps=sa_vec_try_remove panic=86

async / await Compared (Including an Important Correction)

This is a section that was rewritten in the comparison documents. v0.1 once said “the lexicon exists, the runtime is unfinished”, and v0.2 (2026-06-15) corrected it, based on measured test files, to “it is usable in itself; what is missing is the runtime ecosystem”. As of 2026-09-03, a source audit further confirmed: the compiler already has several dedicated continuation/state-machine lowerings, but there is still no general N-await lowering or a Tokio-equivalent runtime.

FeatureRustSLA current
async fn syntaxYesLanded
.await operatorYesLanded
Future typeFuture traitfuture<T> type implemented
Awaiting in a synchronous contextNot allowed; needs block_onSupported (the await_from_sync form)
Nested asyncYesForms such as single/double await, join2, and linear three/four consecutive awaits have been verified; nested await across async fn boundaries is still a gap (rosetta 314/315 fail the same way)
Future state machinestd + tokioCompiler continuation/state-machine lowering already covers linear multiple awaits; cross-boundary nesting and a unified executor are still missing
Async runtimetokio / async-stdNo standalone runtime yet (frontend flattening)
Practical usabilityProduction-gradeFixed forms run; production services still lack a unified runtime, scheduling/backpressure, and complete cancellation propagation

The measured evidence is sa_plugin_sla/tests/test_unit_async_await.sla (Appendix C of rust_vs_sla_final_cn.md records, in the v0.2 / 2026-06-15 framing, “4 tests passing”; the current file contains 2 @test blocks): ready futures, explicit future<int> type annotations, and awaiting directly inside an ordinary synchronous function all run.

// tests/test_unit_async_await.sla（节选）
fn await_from_sync() -> int {
    let result = run_async().await;
    return result;
}

@test "explicit future type parses"() {
    let future: future<int> = step_one();
    let result = future.await;
    if result != 1 { panic(2); };
}
Updated verification framing (2026-09-03) The async matrix currently recorded for sa_plugin_sla is native SA 35/35, SLA→SA→VM 35/35, and strict direct SAB 34/35; the only blocker is the stack_alloc + PIN_MUT_NEW + FUTURE_POLL_STATE combination in the thread-pool case. Three or more consecutive awaits still have no general continuation lowering, so these numbers must not be interpreted as a complete async runtime being finished.

Overall Standard Library Comparison

Source: rust_vs_sla_final_cn.md §2.H (v0.2 / 2026-06-15).

CategoryRust std + ecosystemsa_std + plugins
Vec / HashMap / Stringstdsa_std
Box / Rc / Arcstdsa_std macros + layout
RefCell / Cellstdsa_std macros
Mutex / RwLockstdsa_std macros
File IOstdsa_std/io/fs
Networkingstd + tokio + hyper + reqwestsa_plugin_http_server / http_client (SLA goes through plugins)
Timestdsa_std/time
Processesstdsa_std
Regular expressionscrate (regex)sa_std to be added / via plugins
Serializationcrate (serde)sa_std JSON (simplified)
Mathstd + num-series cratessa_std basics
Cryptographycrate (RustCrypto)sa_std + plugins
Databasescrate (sqlx / diesel)sa_plugin_db / dbnet
Brought in via bc2sa—Any Rust crate compiled to .bc → bc2sa → SA → SLA calls (limited to the subset bc2sa supports)

In one sentence, what this table means: SLA does not intend to rewrite the whole ecosystem. Common containers and IO are given directly by sa_std; framework-level capabilities (HTTP, databases) are handed to plugins; wider third-party libraries go through bc2sa bridging (see the The rosetta Comparison Set and the bc2sa Bridge Ecosystem page for details).

How the Standard Library Surface Lands: std_surface.sla_meta

sla_std/std_surface.sla_meta is a pure data file describing the lowering rules for the standard library surface; the SAB backend reads these rule lines generically, so standard library methods can be implemented by imported SA macros, without hard-coding library semantics in Zig. Three design principles (std_surface_metadata_cn.md §1):

  • No compiler branches: there are no special cases such as “if type == Vec”; everything goes through rule lines;
  • Macro-first: each rule points to an sa_std macro, and the compiler is only responsible for composition;
  • Generic consumer: the SAB backend reads all rule lines in a uniform format and does not dispatch by type name.

There are 8 kinds of rule lines in total:

Rule kindCorresponding call formExample
associatedType::func(args)Vec::new → VEC_NEW
methodvalue.method(args)Option::is_some → OPTION_IS_SOME
functionfunc(recv, args)len(v) → VEC_LEN
fallible_methodFallible method (checks the ok register)Vec::remove → VEC_REMOVE + panic=86
indexvalue[index]VEC_GET_TYPED_{elem_ty}
index_address&value[index]VEC_GET_MUT_PTR_U64
index_assignvalue[index] = valVEC_SET_TYPED
constructorConstruction matched by return typeSome(x) → OPTION_NEW_SOME

{elem_ty} is a template parameter, replaced at compile time with the actual element type name (e.g. i32 → VEC_GET_TYPED_I32). The constraints for adding new rules are written in the same document: no branching on type names, prefer template parameters, only add rules proven necessary by a failing test, and deps= must list all helper macros.
